findings.title: Login-list invalidation uses wrapped isEnabled as membership
findings.body: update() takes the pre-image from getById() (line 91) and passes it to registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate. With the organization feature on, getById() returns the organization-aware wrapper whose isEnabled() is false unless the IdP is enabled and its organization exists, the organization provider is enabled, and the organization itself is enabled. LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() applies ENABLED via IdentityProviderModel::isEnabled, so that override runs. The login list is filled from the JPA delegate's getForLogin, which filters only stored enabled / link-only / hide-on-login plus organization id and kc.org.broker.public, not organization enabled state. If an org-linked IdP is updated while its organization is disabled or missing, the wrapped original already fails the predicate. If the update also makes the raw model ineligible (hide-on-login, link-only, disabled, or broker-public turned off), both sides fail and the method returns without invalidating the .idp.login.* keys. The id stays in the cached set. A later getForLogin expands those ids with getById and does not re-apply hide-on-login, link-only, broker-public, or organization-id checks. OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only re-checks isEnabled(). After the organization is enabled again, that broker is shown on the login page even though it was configured as hidden, link-only, or not public, and getForLogin breaks its contract. The same skip happens when the organization feature is off if the caller mutates the instance returned by getByAlias/getById and passes it to update(): createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel then returns the cached model without copying, so the before/after comparison sees only the new state. Load the pre-image from the JPA delegate (raw flags, not the wrapper) or always invalidate the login keys, and drop resolved models that no longer match the requested mode. testCacheIDPForLogin never updates an org-linked login IdP while the org is disabled, so this is untested.

findings.title: Cached getForLogin results have unstable order
findings.body: getForLogin stores delegate ids with Collectors.toSet() and, on a hit, copies them into another HashSet before returning identityProviders.stream(). Set iteration order is undefined and can change between requests even when membership is unchanged. The previous implementation was the interface default, which returned the delegate getAllStream order. OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean sorts that stream with IDP_COMPARATOR_INSTANCE; List.sort is stable, so providers that compare equal (the usual case when guiOrder is unset or tied, if the comparator has no unique tiebreaker) keep this random order and can swap on the login page on every load. Callers that do not sort lose the previous query order entirely. Cache and return the ids in encounter order (List or LinkedHashSet), not a HashSet.

findings.title: Login-cache test never removes the IdPs it creates
findings.body: testCacheIDPForLogin registers cleanup as testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove (line 381 inside the create loop, and again at line 425) instead of the alias just created (idp-alias-N). The method reference is bound to a proxy for the literal alias "alias", so the 20 providers this test creates are never removed, and cleanup may DELETE a non-existent alias. This class does not otherwise delete those brokers: onAfter only removes a user named member. The new test links ten of them to whichever organization getAll().get(0) returns and asserts exact login-cache sizes (5, 10, 11). Leftover public enabled IdPs change those counts on another run and will also change testCacheIDPByOrg, which asserts an exact getByOrganization size of 6 for the same organization. The new test is therefore order-dependent on the pre-existing leak in testCacheIDPByOrg (same wrong "alias" cleanup). Clean up each created alias (and unlink org brokers) so the realm is isolated.
